content: 1. A study conducted in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, compared the prevalence of tuberculosis in patients with and without HIV infection. The findings were published in the European Journal of Clinical Microbiology & Infectious Diseases in 2005. 2. Patel and Voigt investigated the prevalence and interaction of hepatitis B and latent tuberculosis among Vietnamese immigrants to the United States. Their research was published in the American Journal of Gastroenterology in 2002. 3. Sirinak and colleagues examined the risk factors and treatment outcomes of tuberculosis associated with viral hepatitis and HIV in Thailand. Their findings were published in BMC Public Health in 2008. 4. Padmapriyadarsini and colleagues studied the co-infection of hepatitis B or C in individuals with HIV and the impact of anti-tuberculosis drugs on liver function. This research was published in the Journal of Postgraduate Medicine in 2006. 5. Tassopoulos and colleagues described the natural history of acute hepatitis B surface antigen-positive hepatitis in Greek adults. Their findings were published in Gastroenterology in 1987. 6. Tillmann and colleagues evaluated the safety and efficacy of lamivudine in patients with severe acute or fulminant hepatitis B through a multicenter study. The results were published in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2006. 7. Neumann and colleagues reported on the use of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate in cases of severe acute hepatitis B. Their findings were published in the journal Zeitschrift für Gastroenterologie in 2008. 8. Tillmann, Zachou, and Dalekos discussed the management of severe acute to fulminant hepatitis B, focusing on the decision-making process regarding treatment initiation. Their work was published in Liver International in 2012. 9. Jonas and colleagues reviewed the treatment of children with chronic hepatitis B virus infection in the United States, emphasizing patient selection and therapeutic options. Their findings were published in Hepatology in 2010. 10. Jonas and the International Pediatric Lamivudine Investigator Group studied the long-term use of lamivudine in children with chronic hepatitis B, focusing on the durability of therapeutic responses and safety. This research was published in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2008. 11. Jonas, Kelly, and colleagues evaluated the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of adefovir dipivoxil in children and adolescents aged 2 to <18 years with chronic hepatitis B. Their findings were published in Hepatology in 2008. 12. Sokal and colleagues investigated the pharmacokinetics and safety of adefovir dipivoxil in children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis B virus infection. Their research was published in the Journal of Clinical Pharmacology in 2008. 13. The Weekly Epidemiological Record in 2009 provided an overview of hepatitis B vaccines, including their development and implementation. 14. Graham and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the prevalence of chronic hepatitis B among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians following universal vaccination. Their findings were published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2013. 15. Batham performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the prevalence of hepatitis B in India. The results were published in Indian Pediatrics in 2007. 16. Scott reviewed the burden of chronic liver disease among Aboriginal populations in North America. This work was published in the World Journal of Gastroenterology in 2008. 17. McMahon explored the epidemiology of viral hepatitis in Arctic populations. The findings were published in the International Journal of Circumpolar Health in 2004. 18. The World Health Organization published a handbook in 2010 on monitoring the building blocks of health systems, providing indicators and measurement strategies. 19. The World Health Organization also released a framework in 2010 for developing national health policies, strategies, and plans.
